# Sirach Chapter 26 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 26 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**Council Notes:**
Chapter 26 is the counterpart to ch. 25's negative wife material. The chapter begins with warm praise of the good wife (vv. 1-4, 13-18) — one of the more beautiful passages in Sirach — then includes more negative material on the bad wife (vv. 5-12). The chapter transitions at v. 19 into advice about preserving one's own vitality, then closes with further antithetical wife comparisons (vv. 22-26) and a two/three grief-proverb (v. 27). Vv. 28-29 (bracketed) are an early insertion from the merchant theme of ch. 27.

The imagery of vv. 16-18 (sun, lampstand, golden pillars) is among the most poetically elevated in Sirach and represents the good wife as a figure of cosmic order and sacred beauty.

---

**26:1** Blessed is the husband of a good wife; the number of his days will be doubled.

**26:2** A capable wife brings joy to her husband, and he will complete his years in peace.

**26:3** A good wife is a good portion; she is given in the lot of those who fear the LORD.

**26:4** Whether rich or poor, his heart is glad and his face is cheerful at all times.

**26:5** Three things caused my heart to fear, and a fourth made me prostrate myself: malicious slander in a city, the gathering of a mob, and a false accusation — all these are worse than death;

**26:6** but grief of heart and sorrow is a jealous wife who rivals another, and a lashing tongue that makes everything known to all.

**26:7** An evil wife is a chafing yoke; taking hold of her is like grasping a scorpion.

**26:8** A drunken wife arouses great anger, and she will not cover her own shame.

**26:9** The unchastity of a woman shows in the upward glance of her eyes, and she is recognized by her eyelids.

**26:10** Over a headstrong daughter keep strict watch, lest she find for herself an opportunity of looseness.

**26:11** Guard against her wandering eye, and do not be surprised if she sins against you.

**26:12** Like a thirsty traveler she will open her mouth and drink from any water near at hand; at every post she will sit down, and to every arrow she will open her quiver.

**26:13** The grace of a wife delights her husband, and her wisdom puts flesh on his bones.

**26:14** A wife who keeps silence is a gift from the LORD, and there is no price for a well-disciplined soul.

**26:15** A modest wife has grace upon grace, and no weight can be set against a continent soul.

**26:16** Like the sun rising in the heights of the LORD — so is the beauty of a good wife in the order of her household.

**26:17** Like the shining of the lamp on the sacred lampstand — so is a beautiful face upon a well-proportioned figure.

**26:18** Like pillars of gold on silver bases — so are beautiful feet upon firm heels.

**26:19** My child, preserve the bloom of your youth in good health, and do not give your strength to strangers.

**26:20** Having sought out a fertile field in all the land, sow it with your own seed, trusting in the quality of your own offspring.

**26:21** Your children who outlive you will be great, having confidence in their good lineage.

**26:22** A hired woman is counted like spit, but a married woman is a tower of death to those who take hold of her.

**26:23** A lawless woman will be given as a portion to a lawless man, but a devout woman is given to a man who fears God.

**26:24** A shameless woman will be put to shame at every turn; but an honorable woman will be held in honor.

**26:25** A lawless woman has no sense of shame; but a woman of honor respects her husband.

**26:26** A woman who honors her husband will be considered wise by all; but one who dishonors him in arrogance will be known to all as godless. A loud-voiced woman is like a trumpet heard at every disturbance; and every man in conflict will lend her his ear.

**26:27** Two things bring grief to my heart, and on account of a third anger comes over me: a warrior suffering under poverty; intelligent men treated as rubbish; one who turns from righteousness to sin — the LORD will prepare him for the sword.

**26:28** [A merchant can scarcely avoid negligence, and a shopkeeper will not be innocent of sin.]

**26:29** [Many have sinned for the sake of gain, and one who seeks to multiply wealth averts his eyes from right.]
